args.query: PTO annual accrual days per year

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
PTO accrues each semi-monthly pay period, 24 periods a year. Each period you earn your annual days divided by 24. You can use PTO as soon as it has accrued.
This means your balance grows steadily through the year rather than arriving all at once on January 1. A new employee can take PTO early in their employment, but only the days already accrued; plan longer breaks for later in the year, when more PTO is available. Your available balance in the HR Portal already allows for days that are pending approval.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Part-time employees earn PTO pro rata. Take the full-time days for your service band, multiply by your scheduled weekly hours divided by 40, and round to the nearest half day. For example, a part-time employee scheduled for 24 hours a week in the 15-day band earns 9 days a year.
If your scheduled hours change during the year, your accrual changes from the next pay period. PTO already accrued is not recalculated. Part-time employees take PTO in the same half-day increments as everyone else, counted against their scheduled working days.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Full-time employees earn PTO according to their completed years of service, counted on January 1 (or from the hire date in the first year). With 0–2 completed years you earn 15 days a year. With 3–5 completed years you earn 20 days a year. With 6 or more completed years you earn 25 days a year. The higher rate starts in the calendar year after you reach the new band.
For example, an engineer who joined Ridgeline four years ago has 4 completed years of service and earns 20 days a year. An engineer who completes their sixth year of service during the year moves to 25 days a year from the following January 1. Service is counted from your hire date on your HR record, and periods of unpaid leave do not reduce it.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
If you are on approved leave that spans December 31, you can carry over up to 10 unused PTO days instead of 5.
This applies to approved leave under the Leave of Absence Policy, such as parental leave, that is in progress on December 31. It is applied automatically when your leave is recorded in the HR Portal; you don't need to request it.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
You can carry over up to 5 unused PTO days into the next calendar year. On December 31, any unused days above the 5-day cap are forfeited.
Forfeited days are not paid out. The HR Portal shows your expected carryover from the autumn onwards, so you can plan to use the rest of your PTO before the end of the year. Carried-over days appear in your balance on January 1 and are used like any other PTO.

args.query: contractors not covered HR policies scope

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: This handbook applies to every Ridgeline employee: full-time, part-time and interns. Contractors are not employees. A contractor is bound only by the Code of Conduct (§4), Health and Safety (§5), Reporting Concerns (§6) and the Information Security & Acceptable Use policy (RSE-SEC-01). Every other matter for a contractor, including time off, pay, benefits and working arrangements, is governed by their contract or agency. Contractors with questions about those matters should contact their agency or Ridgeline contract manager. Ridgeline's other HR policies do not apply to contractors. Managers who work with contractors should make sure the contractor knows which Ridgeline rules bind them: how to behave at work, how to stay safe on site, how to raise a concern and how to handle Ridgeline information and systems. Requests from contractors about anything else, such as taking time off or working from another location, are not decided by the contractor's Ridgeline manager under Ridgeline policy; they are settled under the contractor's own contract, through their agency or Ridgeline contract manager.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Full-time employees (exempt and non-exempt), part-time employees and interns earn PTO under this policy. Contractors do not earn PTO and this policy does not apply to them: their time off is set by their contract or agency, and questions go to their agency or Ridgeline contract manager (RSE-HB-01 §1.2).
Eligibility is based on the Employment Type on your HR record. If your Employment Type changes during the year, for example from intern to full-time, your PTO from that date follows the rules for your new type.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text: Field/site-based employees, interns and contractors are not eligible for a home-office stipend.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Every person at Ridgeline has one Employment Type on their HR record. Full-time, exempt employees work a standard 40-hour week. Full-time, non-exempt (hourly) employees also work 40 hours a week, record their time, and need written pre-approval for overtime (§3.3). Part-time employees are scheduled for 20 to 29 hours a week. Interns join for a fixed internship of no more than 6 months. Contractors are engaged through a contract or agency, are not employees, and are covered only as described in §1.2. Ridgeline's HR policies apply to full-time, part-time and intern employees. Your Employment Type affects many of your entitlements: how much PTO you earn, which benefits you can join, whether you record your hours and whether you can claim a home-office stipend. Each policy says which Employment Types it covers in its header block. You can see your own Employment Type in the HR Portal. If you think it is recorded wrongly, contact the HR Service Desk.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
This policy sets out where Ridgeline employees work: the three Work Arrangements, who can become remote-approved, how to request a change, the rules for working remotely, and temporary remote work away from your usual location. It applies to full-time, part-time and intern employees. Business travel is covered separately by RSE-LOC-01 §2.
Ridgeline believes engineering is best done with time together and time to focus. The arrangements in this policy aim to give teams regular in-person collaboration while allowing flexibility where the work allows it. Managers apply the policy fairly and consistently across their teams, and any questions go to the HR Service Desk.
